title: Low-Level Configuration Knobs Instead of Dynamic Policies
pattern: An interface exports low-level, static configuration parameters (retry intervals, cache sizes, timeouts) to control behavior instead of determining it internally or computing it dynamically.
why_bad: Moves complexity upwards instead of down, forcing administrators or high-level callers to understand low-level transport mechanisms to set appropriate values. These static values cannot adapt to real-time environment changes (e.g., variable network latency) and easily become out of date.
detection: Definition of structs representing low-level mechanisms (network, cache, file I/O) that export primitive numeric fields intended for client tuning.
counterexample: Valid user-defined high-level policies (like explicit priority classifications) passed to a scheduler are acceptable. Marked `Context-dependent`.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 8, "Example: configuration parameters", p. 193, 446-447.
